data.summary: The `vnc` directory defines a self-contained Chromium-over-VNC browser surface container for the sandbox platform (Phase G / design §7). The Dockerfile builds a deliberately minimal image (not based on `sandbox-base`) that only mounts the shared `/root` workspace and joins `sandbox-net`, while `entrypoint.sh` supervises the four cooperating processes (TigerVNC Xvnc, openbox, chromium, and a keep-alive loop) that make a drivable remote desktop possible.

file_insights.name: Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Builds the lightweight VNC/Chromium container image used as a pure browser surface for viewing workspace artifacts and dev servers.
file_insights.source_summary: A Dockerfile using `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` with extensive comments explaining its deliberate divergence from `sandbox-base`. It sets up a minimal image that installs the VNC server, window manager, and Chromium packages, copies `entrypoint.sh`, and defines the container's runtime entrypoint and networking/volume assumptions.
file_insights.detailed_description: This Dockerfile intentionally avoids the heavier `sandbox-base` image because the VNC container is only a browser surface: it reads the shared workspace volume at `/root` and reaches dev servers over `sandbox-net` DNS (e.g. `http://code-server:<port>`). It installs only the minimal graphical stack (TigerVNC, openbox, chromium) needed to run a drivable desktop, keeping the image small and the attack surface narrow. It represents the container-build contract for the Phase G VNC feature.
responsibilities: Define the minimal base image and package set for the VNC/Chromium surface
Install TigerVNC, openbox, and chromium without inheriting sandbox-base tooling
Wire in `entrypoint.sh` as the container start command
Document reliance on the shared `/root` volume and `sandbox-net` DNS

file_insights.name: entrypoint.sh
file_insights.summary: Bash supervisor that launches and keeps alive the Xvnc X server, openbox window manager, and Chromium browser that compose the remote desktop.
file_insights.source_summary: A bash script with a descriptive header comment enumerating the four cooperating processes. It sets up the virtual X display, starts `Xvnc` on `:99` with RFB on localhost only, launches `openbox`, starts `chromium` on that display with appropriate flags, and then blocks to keep the container alive while propagating signals/restarts as needed.
file_insights.detailed_description: This is the runtime entrypoint for the VNC container, responsible for starting the four cooperating processes that make a Chromium desktop drivable from a browser: TigerVNC's `Xvnc` on display `:99` (RFB bound to `127.0.0.1:5900`, no auth, `-localhost`), `openbox` as the window manager, Chromium as the actual browser surface with anti-automation/container-safe flags, and a keep-alive/wait loop. It encodes the Phase G / design §7 architecture decisions directly in shell, so changes here directly affect how the remote browser is exposed and kept running.
responsibilities: Start the TigerVNC Xvnc server on display :99 with localhost-only RFB
Launch the openbox window manager on the same display
Start Chromium on :99 with container/anti-automation friendly flags
Keep the container alive and manage the lifecycle of the child processes
